questions.question: Which cable type supports a maximum length of 100 meters (328 feet) for 10Gbps speeds under optimal conditions?
questions.explanation: Cat 6a supports 10 Gbps speeds up to 100 meters. Standard Cat 6 supports 10 Gbps up to only 55 meters.

questions.question: Which expansion slot standard uses point-to-point serial connections called 'lanes'?
questions.explanation: PCI Express (PCIe) uses dedicated point-to-point serial communication lanes (x1, x4, x8, x16).

questions.question: Which Windows command line utility is used to check and repair file system corruption on a disk drive?
questions.explanation: chkdsk checks the file system and file system metadata of a volume for logical and physical errors.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: What type of RAM is commonly found in modern laptops due to its compact size and lower power consumption?
questions.explanation: SODIMM (Small Outline DIMM) is the standard RAM form factor for laptops and compact devices.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a typical security feature found on modern laptops?
questions.explanation: While biometric readers, TPM chips, and disk encryption are standard on modern laptops, mechanical keyboard locks are outdated.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: A user reports their laptop battery no longer holds a charge. After troubleshooting, you determine the battery needs replacement. What should you do first?
options: Check the manufacturer's specifications for the correct battery model
Replace with any compatible laptop battery
questions.explanation: Always verify the correct battery model from the manufacturer before ordering to ensure compatibility and proper fit.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a laptop's heat sink and cooling fan system?
options: To remove heat from the CPU and GPU
To control humidity inside the laptop
questions.explanation: Heat sinks and cooling fans dissipate heat generated by the CPU, GPU, and other components to prevent thermal damage.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: Which component is responsible for converting DC power from the laptop's power adapter into usable power for internal components?
questions.explanation: The voltage regulator module (VRM) converts and stabilizes DC power from the power adapter for CPU, GPU, and other components.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: A customer's laptop keyboard has several non-responsive keys. What is the most cost-effective troubleshooting step?
options: Check for physical debris under the keyboard
questions.explanation: Checking for debris (dust, liquid damage, crumbs) is the least expensive first step before purchasing a new keyboard.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: What type of storage device is most commonly used in modern laptops for better performance and durability?
questions.explanation: SSDs (Solid State Drives) have become standard in modern laptops due to faster performance, lower power consumption, and better durability.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: Which of the following ports is commonly used to connect external displays to modern laptops?
questions.explanation: HDMI and USB-C (with video support) are the standard ports for connecting external displays to modern laptops.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: A laptop is running hot and the fan is constantly loud. Which of these is the most likely cause?
options: Dust and debris clogging the cooling vents
questions.explanation: Clogged cooling vents reduce airflow, causing the CPU to overheat and the fan to run at high speeds continuously.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: What is the purpose of a Trusted Platform Module (TPM) in a laptop?
options: To provide secure hardware-based cryptographic functions
questions.explanation: TPM provides a secure processing environment for cryptographic operations and secure storage of encryption keys.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: Which laptop component typically has the shortest lifespan and requires replacement most frequently?
questions.explanation: Laptop batteries degrade over time with charge cycles and typically need replacement after 3-5 years of use.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: A user accidentally spilled liquid on their laptop. What should be your immediate response?
options: Power on to check if it still works
Power off immediately and allow it to dry completely
Ignore it if the laptop still works
questions.explanation: Immediately power off the device and allow it to dry to prevent short circuits. Never power on a wet laptop.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: What does BIOS stand for in the context of laptop systems?
questions.explanation: BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) is firmware that initializes hardware before the operating system loads.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: Which security mechanism prevents unauthorized access to a laptop's BIOS settings?
questions.explanation: A BIOS/UEFI password prevents unauthorized users from changing critical boot and security settings.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: What is a Kensington lock used for in laptop security?
options: To physically secure the laptop to a desk
questions.explanation: A Kensington security slot allows a cable lock to physically secure the laptop to a desk or stationary object.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: Which of the following is a common sign of a failing laptop hard drive?
questions.explanation: Clicking, grinding, or beeping sounds indicate possible hard drive mechanical failure and data loss risk.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: A laptop won't power on at all. What should you check first?
options: Verify the power adapter is working and connected
questions.explanation: Always verify power delivery first. Check if the power adapter is functioning and properly connected to the laptop.

questions.question: What type of display technology is commonly used in modern smartphones?
questions.explanation: OLED and AMOLED displays are now standard in modern smartphones due to superior color and contrast quality.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of OLED displays over LCD displays?
options: Better color reproduction and true blacks
questions.explanation: OLED displays produce true blacks by turning off individual pixels, resulting in superior contrast and color accuracy.

questions.question: A tablet screen has dead pixels that won't light up. What is the most likely cause?
options: Hardware failure of the display panel
questions.explanation: Dead pixels are typically caused by hardware failure of the LCD/OLED panel and usually require display replacement.

questions.question: What does the term 'touch digitizer' refer to in mobile devices?
options: The touchscreen sensor layer that detects user input
questions.explanation: The digitizer is the sensor layer beneath the display that detects and interprets touch input.

questions.question: A smartphone screen is cracked but still functional. Should you replace just the glass or the entire display assembly?
options: Depends on the severity and device design
Clean it and use a protective case
questions.explanation: Some devices have replaceable glass, while others require full display assembly replacement. Check manufacturer specifications.

questions.question: What is the typical refresh rate of standard mobile device displays?
questions.explanation: Standard mobile displays typically run at 60 Hz, though high-end phones now offer 120 Hz or higher.

questions.question: Which component is responsible for providing power to the mobile device's backlight?
questions.explanation: A backlight inverter or dedicated power circuit provides the correct voltage to LCD backlights.

questions.question: A mobile device screen has reduced brightness or appears unresponsive. Battery level is 80%. What should you check?
options: Check for screen protection film or debris
questions.explanation: Screen protectors, dust, or fingerprints can reduce touch sensitivity and apparent brightness before considering hardware failure.

questions.question: What type of connector is typically used to attach the display assembly to the device motherboard?
questions.explanation: Flex cable connectors (FPC) are standard for connecting displays to mobile device motherboards.

questions.question: A smartphone display shows vertical lines across the screen. This most likely indicates:
options: Damaged display panel or LCD ribbon cable
questions.explanation: Vertical or horizontal lines typically indicate hardware damage to the display panel or a faulty ribbon cable connection.

questions.question: Which type of charging port has largely replaced micro-USB in modern mobile devices?
questions.explanation: USB-C has become the standard charging port for most Android devices and many other mobile devices due to its reversibility and faster charging.

questions.question: What does the 3.5mm headphone jack on some devices provide?
questions.explanation: The 3.5mm jack is an analog audio connector for wired headphones and speakers.

questions.question: A user damaged the charging port on their mobile device. What is the most appropriate troubleshooting step?
options: Use a force fit charging cable
Inspect the port for physical damage and debris
questions.explanation: First inspect the port for physical damage or debris. You may be able to clean it or need to replace the charging port assembly.

questions.question: Which mobile device accessory is primarily used for data transfer and charging?
questions.explanation: Charging cables provide both power delivery and data transfer capabilities to mobile devices.

questions.question: What can happen if you use an incompatible or low-quality charging cable with a mobile device?
options: Damage to the charging port or battery
questions.explanation: Poor quality cables may not meet safety standards and can damage the charging port, battery, or cause overcharging.

questions.question: Which wireless protocol is most commonly used for connecting peripheral devices like headphones to mobile devices?
questions.explanation: Bluetooth is the standard wireless protocol for connecting mobile peripherals like headphones, speakers, and smartwatches.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a screen protector on a mobile device?
questions.explanation: Screen protectors protect the display from scratches, dust, and minor impacts.

questions.question: A mobile device won't charge using the standard USB cable but works with a different cable. What is most likely the issue?
options: The first cable may be damaged or incompatible
questions.explanation: If charging works with one cable but not another, the original cable is likely damaged or not fully compatible.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a common mobile device port or connectivity feature?
questions.explanation: Mobile devices do not include traditional Ethernet ports. They rely on Wi-Fi and cellular connections for network access.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a mobile device case?
options: Protect the device and improve grip
questions.explanation: Cases provide protection from drops, scratches, and impacts while improving grip and ergonomics.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.4 Mobile Device Connectivity & Application Support
questions.question: Which mobile operating system is based on the Linux kernel?
questions.explanation: Android is built on the Linux kernel and is the most widely used mobile operating system.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.4 Mobile Device Connectivity & Application Support
questions.question: What is the primary advantage of Wi-Fi connectivity for mobile devices compared to cellular?
questions.explanation: Wi-Fi typically offers faster speeds and lower latency than cellular networks in most environments.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.4 Mobile Device Connectivity & Application Support
questions.question: Which technology allows mobile devices to make payments by holding them near a payment terminal?
questions.explanation: NFC enables mobile payment systems by allowing short-range wireless communication with payment terminals.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.4 Mobile Device Connectivity & Application Support
questions.question: What is the purpose of GPS in a mobile device?
questions.explanation: GPS (Global Positioning System) enables location-based services and navigation applications.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.4 Mobile Device Connectivity & Application Support
questions.question: A mobile device cannot connect to mobile data despite having a strong cellular signal. Which should you check first?
options: Check data plan settings and APN configuration
questions.explanation: APN (Access Point Name) settings and data plan availability should be verified before considering hardware issues.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.4 Mobile Device Connectivity & Application Support
questions.question: What does 4G LTE provide compared to 3G cellular networks?
questions.explanation: 4G LTE offers significantly lower latency and faster data speeds than 3G networks.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.4 Mobile Device Connectivity & Application Support
questions.question: Which protocol is used for secure communication between mobile devices and application servers?
questions.explanation: HTTPS and TLS protocols provide encryption for secure mobile application communication.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.4 Mobile Device Connectivity & Application Support
questions.question: A user's mobile device won't connect to Wi-Fi despite correct password entry. What should you try first?
options: Disable Wi-Fi and use cellular only
questions.explanation: Forgetting the network removes cached credentials and allows fresh authentication.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.4 Mobile Device Connectivity & Application Support
questions.question: What is a SIM card used for in mobile devices?
options: Enable cellular network connectivity and identify the user
questions.explanation: The SIM (Subscriber Identity Module) card identifies the user to the carrier and enables cellular network access.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.4 Mobile Device Connectivity & Application Support
questions.question: A mobile application constantly crashes after an update. What is the most appropriate troubleshooting step?
questions.explanation: Uninstalling and reinstalling the application clears corrupted cache/data from the update without affecting other apps or system data.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: Which expansion card is primarily used for adding additional USB ports to a laptop?
questions.explanation: USB expansion cards can be added via external connections to increase available USB ports on a laptop.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: What is the purpose of laptop dock/docking station?
options: Provide additional connectivity and ease of connection to peripherals
questions.explanation: Docking stations provide quick connection to multiple peripherals (monitors, keyboards, network) without individual cable connections.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 1.1 Laptop Hardware, Components & Physical Security
questions.question: A laptop randomly shuts down under load. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Random shutdowns under load typically indicate thermal issues causing the system to shut down as a safety mechanism.

questions.question: Which OSI layer is responsible for routing data between different networks?
questions.explanation: The Network Layer (Layer 3) is responsible for routing and forwarding data between different networks using IP addresses.

questions.question: What does TCP stand for in networking?
questions.explanation: TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) is a connection-oriented protocol that ensures reliable data delivery.

questions.question: Which protocol is connectionless and does not guarantee packet delivery?
questions.explanation: UDP (User Datagram Protocol) is connectionless and does not ensure packet delivery, making it faster but less reliable than TCP.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the DHCP protocol?
options: Automatically assign IP addresses to devices
Translate domain names to IP addresses
questions.explanation: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) automatically assigns IP addresses and network configuration to devices on a network.

questions.question: Which protocol is used to resolve domain names to IP addresses?
questions.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) translates human-readable domain names into IP addresses.

questions.question: What does HTTP stand for?
questions.explanation: HTTP (Hyper Text Transfer Protocol) is the unsecured protocol used for web communication.

questions.question: Which protocol provides secure web communication and encrypts data in transit?
questions.explanation: HTTPS is HTTP with SSL/TLS encryption to secure communications between client and server.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the ICMP protocol?
options: Send diagnostic messages and ping requests
questions.explanation: ICMP (Internet Control Message Protocol) is used for network diagnostics like ping and traceroute.

questions.question: Which protocol is used for sending email?
questions.explanation: SMTP (Simple Mail Transfer Protocol) is used for sending emails from clients to mail servers.

questions.question: What protocol is used for retrieving emails from a mail server?
questions.explanation: POP3 and IMAP are protocols for retrieving emails. IMAP is more modern and supports multiple folders.

questions.question: Which protocol is used for remote secure shell access to systems?
questions.explanation: SSH (Secure Shell) provides secure encrypted remote command-line access to systems.

questions.question: What does ARP stand for?
questions.explanation: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) maps IP addresses to MAC addresses on a local network.

questions.question: Which protocol manages network devices and collects information about their status?
questions.explanation: SNMP (Simple Network Management Protocol) monitors and manages network devices.

questions.question: A computer cannot reach a server on a different network. Which protocol would you use to diagnose the connection?
questions.explanation: ICMP (ping) is used to test connectivity and diagnose network routing issues.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a network hub?
options: Repeat signals to all connected ports
questions.explanation: A hub is a central connection point that repeats all signals to all connected ports, creating one collision domain.

questions.question: What is a key advantage of a network switch over a hub?
options: Creates separate collision domains per port
questions.explanation: Switches create separate collision domains for each port, reducing collisions and improving performance.

questions.question: Which device is used to connect different networks and can filter traffic based on IP addresses?
questions.explanation: A router connects different networks and uses IP addresses to route packets between them.

questions.question: What does a network bridge do?
options: Connects network segments and filters based on MAC addresses
questions.explanation: A bridge connects LAN segments and uses MAC addresses to filter traffic, creating separate collision domains.

questions.question: Which networking device amplifies wireless signals to extend network coverage?
questions.explanation: A wireless extender or repeater receives and rebroadcasts wireless signals to extend coverage area.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a modem?
options: Convert digital signals to analog and vice versa
questions.explanation: A modem modulates/demodulates digital computer signals to analog signals for transmission over phone or cable lines.

questions.question: Which networking device is typically used to provide wireless connectivity in a home or office?
questions.explanation: An access point or wireless router provides Wi-Fi connectivity to client devices.

questions.question: A network device only broadcasts ARP requests without responding. What is most likely wrong?
options: Device is isolated and not on same subnet
questions.explanation: When a device cannot reach others via ARP, it typically means the device is on a different subnet or isolated network.

questions.question: What does 802.11 refer to?
questions.explanation: 802.11 is the IEEE standard for wireless LAN (WLAN) communications.

questions.question: Which Wi-Fi standard offers the fastest speeds in the 5 GHz band?
questions.explanation: 802.11ax (Wi-Fi 6) is the newest and fastest standard, offering speeds up to 9.6 Gbps.

questions.question: What is the maximum range of a typical 802.11n wireless network?
questions.explanation: 802.11n typically has a range of approximately 300 feet indoors in optimal conditions.

questions.question: Which wireless security protocol should NOT be used due to known vulnerabilities?
questions.explanation: WEP (Wired Equivalent Privacy) has serious security vulnerabilities and should never be used.

questions.question: What does WPA stand for in wireless security?
questions.explanation: WPA (Wi-Fi Protected Access) provides stronger encryption than WEP and is still widely used.

questions.question: A wireless device connects to the network but cannot access the internet. Which is most likely the issue?
options: Default gateway or router not configured
questions.explanation: Without a default gateway, the device cannot route traffic beyond the local network.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a RADIUS server in network authentication?
questions.explanation: RADIUS (Remote Authentication Dial-In User Service) provides centralized authentication for network access control.

questions.question: What does NTP stand for?
questions.explanation: NTP (Network Time Protocol) synchronizes time across network devices to maintain accurate timestamps.

questions.question: Which service provides directory services and centralized user authentication for Windows networks?
questions.explanation: Active Directory provides centralized authentication, authorization, and directory services for Windows domain networks.

questions.question: What is the primary function of a VPN?
options: Create an encrypted tunnel for secure remote access
questions.explanation: A VPN (Virtual Private Network) creates an encrypted connection to a private network over the internet.

questions.question: Which protocol is commonly used for VPN connections?
questions.explanation: OpenVPN and IPSec are common protocols used for establishing secure VPN connections.

questions.question: Which of these is an unshielded twisted pair cable?
questions.explanation: UTP (Unshielded Twisted Pair) is the most common Ethernet cable without metal shielding.

questions.question: What is the maximum recommended distance for Cat 6 cables at Gigabit speeds?
questions.explanation: Cat 6 cables support Gigabit speeds up to 100 meters (compared to 55 meters for 10 Gbps).

questions.question: Which connector type is used for fiber optic cables?
questions.explanation: ST and LC connectors are common types for fiber optic cable connections.

questions.question: What is an advantage of fiber optic cables over copper cables?
options: Immunity to electromagnetic interference and higher speeds
questions.explanation: Fiber optic cables are immune to EMI interference and support much higher speeds and longer distances than copper.

questions.question: A network cable is labeled 'Cat 5e.' What is the maximum data rate it can support?
questions.explanation: Cat 5e supports up to 1 Gbps (Gigabit Ethernet) at maximum distances of 100 meters.

questions.question: What does CIDR notation like /24 represent?
questions.explanation: /24 indicates that 24 bits are used for the network portion of the IP address, leaving 8 bits for hosts.

questions.question: What is the subnet mask for a /25 CIDR block?
questions.explanation: /25 means 25 network bits, leaving 7 host bits, resulting in a subnet mask of 255.255.255.128.

questions.question: What is a default gateway?
options: First IP address on the network
Router that forwards packets to other networks
questions.explanation: The default gateway is the router that handles traffic destined for other networks.

questions.question: A computer has IP address 192.168.1.50 with subnet mask 255.255.255.0. What is the network address?
questions.explanation: The network address is determined by ANDing the IP address with the subnet mask, resulting in 192.168.1.0.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 2.7 Internet Connection Types & Network Types
questions.question: Which internet connection type uses telephone lines and is the slowest?
questions.explanation: Dial-up is the oldest and slowest internet connection method, with speeds up to 56 kbps.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 2.7 Internet Connection Types & Network Types
questions.question: Which internet connection type typically offers speeds between 5-25 Mbps over cable infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Cable internet (via cable modem) typically offers speeds between 5-25 Mbps or higher depending on the plan.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 2.7 Internet Connection Types & Network Types
questions.question: What is a major disadvantage of satellite internet?
questions.explanation: Satellite internet has high latency due to signal travel distance to satellites in orbit, affecting real-time applications.

questions.question: Which command is used to test connectivity between two hosts?
questions.explanation: The ping command sends ICMP echo requests to test if a host is reachable.

questions.question: What does the 'ipconfig' command display?
options: Network device configuration and IP settings
questions.explanation: ipconfig displays local network configuration including IP address, subnet mask, and gateway.

questions.question: Which command shows the route that packets take to reach a destination?
questions.explanation: tracert (Windows) and traceroute (Linux) show the path packets take through multiple hops to reach a destination.

questions.question: What does 'nslookup' command do?
options: Query DNS servers for IP address of a domain
questions.explanation: nslookup queries DNS servers to resolve domain names to IP addresses.

questions.question: A user cannot reach a website by domain name but can reach it by IP address. What is the most likely issue?
questions.explanation: If IP works but domain name doesn't, the DNS server is not properly resolving the domain name.

questions.question: Which layer of the OSI model deals with physical transmission of data?
questions.explanation: The Physical Layer (Layer 1) handles the actual transmission of bits over physical media like cables.

questions.question: Which connector type is used for legacy parallel devices on traditional desktop computers?
questions.explanation: DB-25 and Centronics connectors were standard for parallel connections to printers and other devices.

questions.question: What does SATA stand for?
questions.explanation: SATA (Serial ATA) is the standard interface for connecting hard drives and SSDs to motherboards.

questions.question: Which power connector is used to supply power to the CPU on modern motherboards?
questions.explanation: Modern CPUs require dedicated 8-pin or 4-pin CPU power connectors for adequate power delivery.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of the 24-pin ATX main power connector?
options: Deliver main power to the motherboard and all components
questions.explanation: The 24-pin ATX connector provides primary power distribution to the entire motherboard.

questions.question: Which cable type uses twisted pairs and is shielded to reduce electromagnetic interference?
questions.explanation: STP (Shielded Twisted Pair) includes protective shielding to minimize electromagnetic interference.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a eSATA (External SATA) connector?
questions.explanation: eSATA allows external SATA drives to be connected to a computer from outside the case.

questions.question: What does RAM stand for?
questions.explanation: RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile memory used for temporary storage during system operation.

questions.question: What type of RAM is most commonly used in modern desktop computers?
questions.explanation: DDR4 is currently the most common RAM type in desktop systems, though DDR5 is becoming more prevalent.

questions.question: How many memory slots are typically available on a standard ATX motherboard?
questions.explanation: Most ATX motherboards have 4 DIMM slots, allowing up to 4 memory modules to be installed.

questions.question: A computer is running slowly and experiencing lag. A technician checks and the system has 2GB of RAM. What is likely the issue?
questions.explanation: 2GB of RAM is very low for modern operating systems and applications, causing excessive disk paging and slowness.

questions.question: What is the purpose of RAM speed (measured in MHz)?
options: Speed at which data is accessed and processed
questions.explanation: RAM speed determines how quickly data can be read from and written to memory, affecting overall system performance.

questions.question: A system with 16GB of RAM and a 256GB SSD is unable to boot. What should be checked first?
options: Check RAM module seating and connections
questions.explanation: If modules fail to post, first check that RAM is properly seated in the DIMM slots.

questions.question: What does SSD stand for?
questions.explanation: SSD (Solid State Drive) uses flash memory and has no moving parts, offering faster speeds than mechanical drives.

questions.question: What is the typical rotational speed of a 'fast' enterprise hard disk drive?
questions.explanation: Enterprise HDDs typically spin at 10,000 to 15,000 RPM for improved performance compared to consumer drives.

questions.question: Compared to HDDs, what is the main advantage of SSDs?
questions.explanation: SSDs offer dramatically faster read/write speeds and lower latency compared to traditional hard disk drives.

questions.question: What type of interface does an M.2 NVMe SSD use for connecting to the motherboard?
questions.explanation: M.2 NVMe drives use the PCIe interface, providing much faster speeds than SATA SSDs.

questions.question: A user reports their computer is very slow despite having significant free disk space. What is likely the issue?
questions.explanation: On HDDs, severe fragmentation can cause slowness even with free space available. SSDs don't suffer from fragmentation.

questions.question: What is RAID used for in storage systems?
options: Increase reliability through redundancy or performance through striping
questions.explanation: RAID (Redundant Array of Independent Disks) improves performance via striping and reliability via mirroring/parity.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 3.4 Install Configure Motherboards CPU Expansion Cards
questions.question: What does CPU stand for?
questions.explanation: CPU (Central Processing Unit) is the primary processor that executes instructions and performs calculations.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 3.4 Install Configure Motherboards CPU Expansion Cards
questions.question: Which socket type is commonly used for modern Intel processors?
questions.explanation: LGA 1700 (Land Grid Array) is used for modern Intel 12th generation and newer processors.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 3.4 Install Configure Motherboards CPU Expansion Cards
questions.question: Which CPU socket is commonly used for AMD Ryzen processors?
questions.explanation: AM4 socket is used for AMD Ryzen mainstream processors from multiple generations.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 3.4 Install Configure Motherboards CPU Expansion Cards
questions.question: What is a CPU cooler/heatsink primarily responsible for?
options: Dissipate heat from the CPU to prevent thermal damage
questions.explanation: CPU coolers transfer heat from the processor to air or liquid for dissipation, preventing thermal shutdown.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 3.4 Install Configure Motherboards CPU Expansion Cards
questions.question: What does integrated graphics mean?
options: Graphics card is built into the CPU
questions.explanation: Integrated graphics are GPU cores built directly into the CPU, eliminating the need for a discrete graphics card.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 3.4 Install Configure Motherboards CPU Expansion Cards
questions.question: Which expansion card type provides the fastest data transfer speeds?
questions.explanation: PCIe x16 slots provide the highest bandwidth for graphics cards and high-speed expansion cards.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 3.4 Install Configure Motherboards CPU Expansion Cards
questions.question: What is the purpose of a GPU (Graphics Processing Unit)?
options: Process and render graphics and video
questions.explanation: GPUs are specialized processors optimized for rendering graphics, video, and parallel computations.

questions.question: What does PSU stand for?
questions.explanation: PSU (Power Supply Unit) converts AC power from the wall to DC power for computer components.

questions.question: What is the ATX power rating used for?
options: Show the maximum power a PSU can deliver
questions.explanation: PSU wattage (e.g., 650W, 850W) indicates the maximum power output available for all system components.

questions.question: A system with a high-end GPU and CPU requires significant power. What minimum PSU wattage would you recommend?
questions.explanation: High-end systems need adequate PSU capacity for stability, typically requiring 850W or more.

questions.question: What is a common sign of power supply failure?
options: System randomly shuts down or won't power on
Screen flickering only during video playback
questions.explanation: Failing PSUs typically cause unexpected shutdowns, no-power conditions, or system instability.

questions.question: What does a UPS (Uninterruptible Power Supply) provide?
options: Increased AC power from the wall
Battery backup power during outages and surge protection
questions.explanation: A UPS provides temporary battery power during outages and protects equipment from power surges.

questions.question: What is a multifunction device (MFD)?
options: Multiple hard drives in one unit
A device that combines printing, scanning, copying, and faxing
Multiple network ports on one card
questions.explanation: Multifunction devices combine multiple functions like printing, scanning, copying, and faxing in one unit.

questions.question: What is the primary advantage of using an MFD in an office environment?
options: Cost savings by replacing multiple devices with one
questions.explanation: MFDs reduce costs and space by combining multiple office devices into a single unit.

questions.question: Which type of connection is most commonly used to connect an MFD to a network?
questions.explanation: Modern MFDs typically use Ethernet for network connectivity, allowing shared access from multiple users.

questions.question: An MFD is not able to receive fax jobs. What should you check first?
options: Check phone line connection and settings
questions.explanation: Fax functionality requires proper phone line connection and correct fax settings configuration.

questions.question: What types of printers are most commonly used in modern offices?
questions.explanation: Inkjet printers are used for home/small office color printing, while laser printers are standard for high-volume office use.

questions.question: A laser printer produces blurry prints with low contrast. What is the most likely cause?
questions.explanation: Fusing unit problems or temperature issues cause poor print quality, low contrast, and smudging.

questions.question: How often should laser printer maintenance be performed?
options: Every 5000 pages or as specified by manufacturer
Only when there is a problem
questions.explanation: Laser printers require regular maintenance (every 5000-50,000 pages) to replace consumables and maintain quality.

questions.question: A printer is printing blank pages. Which component is most likely the issue?
options: Toner cartridge is empty or improperly installed
questions.explanation: Blank pages typically indicate the toner cartridge is empty, not installed properly, or needs the seal removed.

questions.question: What are the main consumable components in a laser printer that require regular replacement?
questions.explanation: Toner cartridges and fuser units are the primary consumables that require periodic replacement in laser printers.

questions.question: An inkjet printer produces streaky color output. What should you do first?
questions.explanation: Print head clogs cause streaky output and can be fixed with the printer's built-in cleaning function.

questions.question: What is the purpose of thermal paste on a CPU cooler?
options: Improve heat transfer between CPU and cooler
questions.explanation: Thermal paste fills microscopic imperfections between the CPU and cooler to maximize heat transfer.

questions.question: What is the difference between DIMM and SODIMM form factors?
options: DIMM is for desktops, SODIMM is for laptops
questions.explanation: DIMM (Dual In-line Memory Module) is used in desktops, while SODIMM (Small Outline DIMM) is used in laptops.

questions.question: What does the 'S' in SATA stand for?
questions.explanation: Serial ATA transmits data one bit at a time in a serial fashion, unlike the parallel IDE it replaced.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 3.4 Install Configure Motherboards CPU Expansion Cards
questions.question: What is overclocking?
options: Running CPU at higher clock speeds than rated
questions.explanation: Overclocking increases CPU frequency beyond factory settings to achieve higher performance, but risks instability.

questions.question: A power supply makes fan noise. Is this a problem?
options: Normal as PSU fans vary speed based on load
questions.explanation: PSU fans adjust speed based on internal temperature and load, so noise variation is normal.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 3.4 Install Configure Motherboards CPU Expansion Cards
questions.question: A computer won't boot and shows no signs of power. Which component should be tested first?
questions.explanation: Always verify power delivery by testing the PSU when a system shows no signs of power or life.

questions.question: What is the advantage of NVMe over SATA SSDs?
questions.explanation: NVMe drives use the PCIe interface, providing speeds up to 5-7 times faster than SATA SSDs.

questions.question: A Molex connector is primarily used for what purpose?
options: Power delivery to IDE drives and other legacy components
questions.explanation: Molex 4-pin connectors provide 12V and 5V power to legacy IDE drives and expansion cards.

questions.question: A system freezes randomly. After reseating RAM, the issue persists. What should you try next?
questions.explanation: Use memory diagnostic tools to check for RAM errors when system freezing is reseating doesn't fix.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 3.4 Install Configure Motherboards CPU Expansion Cards
questions.question: What is the purpose of the BIOS on a motherboard?
options: Initialize hardware before OS boot and provide system settings
questions.explanation: BIOS (Basic Input/Output System) performs hardware initialization and provides low-level configuration options.

questions.question: What does 80+ Bronze rating on a power supply mean?
questions.explanation: 80+ Bronze means the PSU achieves at least 80% efficiency at 50% load, reducing wasted energy as heat.

questions.question: What is virtualization?
options: Running the internet on a computer
Creating virtual versions of physical computers using software
questions.explanation: Virtualization uses software to create virtual machines that act as independent computers on physical hardware.

questions.question: What is a hypervisor?
options: Software that manages and runs virtual machines
questions.explanation: A hypervisor (or virtual machine monitor) is software that creates, runs, and manages virtual machines on physical hardware.

questions.question: What is the difference between Type 1 and Type 2 hypervisors?
options: Type 1 is faster but Type 2 is cheaper
Type 1 runs directly on hardware, Type 2 runs on an OS
questions.explanation: Type 1 hypervisors run directly on hardware (bare-metal), while Type 2 runs on top of a host OS.

questions.question: What is cloud computing?
options: Using the internet for weather forecasting
On-demand access to computing resources via the internet
questions.explanation: Cloud computing provides on-demand access to computing resources (servers, storage, software) over the internet.

questions.question: What does SaaS stand for?
questions.explanation: SaaS (Software as a Service) delivers applications over the internet, like Google Workspace or Microsoft 365.

questions.question: What does IaaS stand for?
questions.explanation: IaaS (Infrastructure as a Service) provides virtual computing resources over the internet, like AWS or Azure.

questions.question: What does PaaS stand for?
questions.explanation: PaaS (Platform as a Service) provides development platforms and tools in the cloud for building applications.

questions.question: What is private cloud computing?
options: Cloud infrastructure dedicated to a single organization
questions.explanation: Private cloud is cloud infrastructure dedicated to a single organization, providing more control and security.

questions.question: What is public cloud computing?
options: Cloud services provided to the general public over the internet
questions.explanation: Public cloud is cloud infrastructure and services available to anyone, managed by providers like AWS, Azure, or Google Cloud.

questions.question: What is hybrid cloud?
options: Combination of private and public cloud resources
questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud integrates private and public cloud resources, allowing organizations to balance control and scalability.

questions.question: What is a primary advantage of cloud computing for businesses?
options: Scalability and reduced upfront infrastructure costs
questions.explanation: Cloud computing provides scalability, flexibility, and reduces capital expenditure on infrastructure.

questions.question: What security concern exists with cloud computing?
options: Data is stored on provider's servers outside direct control
questions.explanation: Cloud security concerns include data residency, compliance, and trust in the provider's security practices.

questions.question: What is a virtual machine (VM)?
options: A software-based computer running on physical hardware
A backup of a real computer
A type of cloud service only
questions.explanation: A virtual machine is a software emulation of a physical computer that runs an OS and applications independently.

questions.question: What is a snapshot in virtual machine management?
options: A saved state of a VM at a specific point in time
questions.explanation: A snapshot captures the VM's state (memory, disk, settings) at a specific moment, allowing quick restoration.

questions.question: What is VM migration?
options: Moving a VM to another country
Moving a running VM from one physical host to another with no downtime
questions.explanation: VM migration moves virtual machines between physical hosts, useful for load balancing and maintenance.

questions.question: What resource allocation issue might occur with virtual machines?
options: Over-provisioning resources to VMs can reduce host performance
VMs always perform better than physical computers
questions.explanation: Over-allocating resources to too many VMs can exceed host capacity, causing performance degradation.

questions.question: What is the purpose of VM templates?
options: Preconfigured VM images for quickly creating new VMs
questions.explanation: Templates provide standardized, preconfigured VM images, accelerating deployment and ensuring consistency.

questions.question: What is cloning a virtual machine?
options: Creating an exact copy of an existing VM
questions.explanation: Cloning creates identical copies of a VM, useful for creating multiple instances or backups.

questions.question: A VM is running slowly despite adequate host resources. What should you check first?
options: Check VM resource allocation and host performance metrics
questions.explanation: Verify VM resource allocation and monitor host metrics to identify bottlenecks before making changes.

questions.question: What is the advantage of using a dedicated VM for testing software?
options: Testing faster than on physical computers
Isolated environment prevents affecting production systems
questions.explanation: VMs provide isolated, disposable test environments that don't risk production data or systems.

questions.question: What hypervisor is commonly used in Windows environments?
questions.explanation: Hyper-V is Microsoft's hypervisor for Windows Server environments, built into Windows Pro and Enterprise editions.

questions.question: What hypervisor is commonly used in Linux environments?
questions.explanation: KVM is a Linux kernel module that enables virtualization on Linux systems without additional hypervisor software.

questions.question: What is containerization?
options: Lightweight virtualization that packages applications with dependencies
questions.explanation: Containers package applications with their dependencies in isolated environments, similar to VMs but more efficient.

questions.question: What is Docker?
options: A containerization platform for building and running containers
questions.explanation: Docker is a containerization platform that simplifies creating, deploying, and managing containers.

questions.question: What is the main difference between containers and VMs?
options: Containers are lighter and faster, sharing the host OS kernel vs VMs having separate OS instances
VMs are better for all purposes
questions.explanation: Containers share the host OS kernel, making them smaller and faster than VMs, but less isolated.

questions.question: What is load balancing in cloud environments?
options: Distributing user traffic across multiple servers for performance and reliability
questions.explanation: Load balancing distributes incoming traffic across multiple servers, improving performance and providing redundancy.

questions.question: What is auto-scaling in cloud computing?
options: Automatically adjusting resources based on demand
questions.explanation: Auto-scaling automatically increases or decreases resources based on current demand, optimizing cost and performance.

questions.question: What is an API in cloud services?
options: Application Programming Interface allowing applications to communicate with cloud services
questions.explanation: APIs allow applications to interact with cloud services programmatically, enabling integration and automation.

questions.question: What is a service level agreement (SLA) in cloud computing?
options: Contractual agreement specifying service uptime, performance, and support guarantees
questions.explanation: An SLA defines provider commitments regarding service availability, performance metrics, and remedies for failures.

questions.question: What is meant by 'cloud provider redundancy'?
options: Multiple data centers ensuring services continue if one fails
questions.explanation: Redundancy means cloud providers maintain multiple data centers so if one becomes unavailable, services continue elsewhere.

questions.question: A company needs to ensure data can be recovered after a disaster. Which cloud feature is most important?
questions.explanation: Disaster recovery and backup services ensure data can be restored after system failures or disasters.

questions.question: When should you use a virtual machine instead of a physical computer?
options: For testing, development, server consolidation, or running multiple OS simultaneously
questions.explanation: VMs are ideal for testing, isolated environments, server consolidation, and running multiple operating systems.

questions.question: What is VM sprawl?
options: Uncontrolled proliferation of underutilized VMs consuming resources
VMs taking up too much storage
questions.explanation: VM sprawl occurs when too many underutilized VMs are created, wasting resources and complicating management.

questions.question: What is the purpose of VM monitoring tools?
options: Track VM performance, resource usage, and health to ensure optimal operation
questions.explanation: Monitoring tools track VM metrics like CPU, memory, disk I/O, and network usage for performance management.

questions.question: A VM fails to start. What is the first troubleshooting step?
options: Check host resources and VM configuration settings
questions.explanation: First verify host has adequate free resources and the VM configuration is correct before more drastic measures.

questions.question: What is the relationship between virtualization and cloud computing?
options: Virtualization is a technology used to enable cloud computing
questions.explanation: Cloud computing relies on virtualization technology to provide flexible, scalable infrastructure to multiple customers.

questions.question: What does 'on-demand' mean in cloud computing?
options: Resources available immediately when needed, paid for actual usage
questions.explanation: On-demand means users can provision resources instantly and pay only for what they use.

questions.question: A business wants to migrate to the cloud but needs to keep some data on-premises. Which cloud model fits best?
questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud combines public and private cloud, allowing sensitive data to stay on-premises while using public cloud for less critical workloads.

questions.question: What is cloud portability?
options: Ability to move applications between different cloud providers
Cloud services that are portable devices
questions.explanation: Cloud portability means applications and data can be moved between cloud providers without major modifications.

questions.question: What is a potential disadvantage of cloud computing?
options: Internet dependency and potential latency issues
questions.explanation: Cloud computing requires reliable internet connectivity and can suffer latency, making it unsuitable for some real-time applications.

questions.question: What is VM performance optimization?
options: Tuning VM resource allocation and host settings to maximize performance
questions.explanation: VM optimization involves proper resource allocation, memory management, and host tuning for best performance.

questions.question: A VM has network connectivity issues. What should you verify first?
options: VM network adapter settings and connectivity configuration
questions.explanation: Verify VM network adapter configuration, virtual network settings, and host network connectivity before hardware changes.

questions.question: What is the cloud computing model called when you only pay for what you use?
questions.explanation: Pay-as-you-go pricing means users are charged based on actual resource consumption rather than fixed subscriptions.

questions.question: What is infrastructure as code (IaC) in cloud environments?
options: Managing infrastructure through code/scripts rather than manual configuration
questions.explanation: IaC allows infrastructure to be defined as code, enabling version control, repeatability, and automated deployment.

questions.question: A company experiences a ransomware attack. Which cloud feature would have prevented data loss?
questions.explanation: Regular automated backups stored separately from production systems allow recovery from ransomware attacks.

questions.question: What file typically contains VM configuration and settings?
options: XML or configuration files specific to the hypervisor
questions.explanation: VM configuration is typically stored in files like .vmx (VMware), .vhdx (Hyper-V), or XML formats.

questions.question: What is data residency in cloud computing?
options: Physical location where data is stored, important for compliance
questions.explanation: Data residency specifies where data must be stored geographically, critical for regulatory compliance (GDPR, CCPA, etc.).

questions.question: What is multi-tenancy in cloud computing?
options: Single cloud application serving multiple customers with isolated data
questions.explanation: Multi-tenancy allows a single cloud application to serve many customers with complete data isolation between them.

questions.question: What is the advantage of using cloud-based backups?
options: Automatic, scalable, geographically distributed backup protection
questions.explanation: Cloud backups provide automatic protection, offsite storage, scalability, and protection against local disasters.

questions.question: A company wants to test a new application without affecting production. What's the best approach?
options: Create a VM or cloud instance for isolated testing
questions.explanation: Virtual or cloud environments provide isolated, disposable test spaces perfect for safely testing applications without production risk.

questions.question: What does VM consolidation mean?
options: Combining multiple physical servers into fewer VMs
Running many VMs on a single physical server
Reducing VM count by moving services onto physical servers
Combining VMs with the same OS
questions.explanation: VM consolidation runs multiple virtual machines on fewer physical servers, improving resource utilization and reducing costs.

questions.question: What is the first step in the troubleshooting methodology?
questions.explanation: The first step is to clearly identify and document the problem, including symptoms and when it occurs.

questions.question: What should you do before making any changes to a system?
options: Establish a baseline and document the current state
questions.explanation: Always establish a baseline of the current system state before making changes so you can revert if needed.

questions.question: What is the purpose of creating backups before troubleshooting?
options: Prevent data loss if troubleshooting causes problems
questions.explanation: Backups protect data in case troubleshooting procedures accidentally cause data loss or system failure.

questions.question: When testing a potential solution, what approach is best?
options: Change one thing at a time and test results
Test everything on a production system
questions.explanation: Change one variable at a time so you can identify which change actually fixed the problem.

questions.question: What should you do if your troubleshooting doesn't solve the problem?
options: Escalate or research further based on findings
questions.explanation: If initial troubleshooting doesn't work, escalate to higher-level support or research more complex causes.

questions.question: What is the purpose of documentation in troubleshooting?
options: Track findings, solutions, and create knowledge for future similar issues
questions.explanation: Documentation creates institutional knowledge and helps technicians solve similar problems faster in the future.

questions.question: What does the 'OSI Model' help with in troubleshooting?
options: Systematically identify networking issues layer by layer
questions.explanation: The OSI model provides a framework to systematically troubleshoot network issues from physical to application layers.

questions.question: What principle suggests you should check obvious things first before complex solutions?
questions.explanation: Occam's Razor principle suggests the simplest explanation is usually correct - check basic things first.

questions.question: A user reports their printer won't print. What's the first troubleshooting step?
options: Check if the printer is on and connected
questions.explanation: Always start with the basics: is the device on, connected, and receiving power?

questions.objective: Core 1 - 5.2 Troubleshooting Motherboards, RAM, CPU & Power
questions.question: A computer won't power on at all. What component should you test first?
questions.explanation: Without power delivery, nothing will work. Test the power supply before other components.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 5.2 Troubleshooting Motherboards, RAM, CPU & Power
questions.question: A system powers on but immediately powers off. What's likely the issue?
questions.explanation: Immediate power-off typically indicates CPU overheating causing thermal protection shutdown.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 5.2 Troubleshooting Motherboards, RAM, CPU & Power
questions.question: What is a POST (Power-On Self Test)?
options: System self-test during startup checking hardware before OS loads
questions.explanation: POST is the BIOS self-test that runs on startup to verify hardware is functional before the OS loads.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 5.2 Troubleshooting Motherboards, RAM, CPU & Power
questions.question: A system produces beep codes during startup but won't boot. What do the beeps indicate?
options: Hardware problem - beep pattern indicates which component
questions.explanation: POST beep codes identify hardware problems: one beep is normal, other patterns indicate specific component failures.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 5.2 Troubleshooting Motherboards, RAM, CPU & Power
questions.question: What does a continuous beep during startup typically indicate?
questions.explanation: Continuous beeping usually indicates RAM is faulty or not properly seated in the DIMM slots.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 5.2 Troubleshooting Motherboards, RAM, CPU & Power
questions.question: A system runs but randomly crashes with no error message. What should you suspect first?
questions.explanation: Random crashes often indicate faulty RAM. Run memory diagnostic tests (Windows Memory Diagnostic, Memtest86).

questions.objective: Core 1 - 5.2 Troubleshooting Motherboards, RAM, CPU & Power
questions.question: A computer shows BIOS but won't boot the OS. What's a good first troubleshooting step?
options: Check boot sequence order in BIOS
questions.explanation: If BIOS shows but OS won't boot, verify boot order is correct - may be trying to boot from wrong device.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 5.2 Troubleshooting Motherboards, RAM, CPU & Power
questions.question: What is CMOS battery on a motherboard responsible for?
options: Maintaining BIOS settings and system time when powered off
questions.explanation: CMOS battery maintains BIOS settings and the system clock when the computer is off.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 5.2 Troubleshooting Motherboards, RAM, CPU & Power
questions.question: A system has wrong date/time that keeps resetting. What's the likely cause?
questions.explanation: CMOS battery failure causes loss of time/date settings and BIOS configuration after power-off.

questions.question: A hard drive makes clicking noises and is not recognized. What does this indicate?
questions.explanation: Clicking/grinding sounds from a hard drive indicate mechanical failure and imminent data loss.

questions.question: An SSD is not detected by the system. What should you check first?
options: Verify SATA/NVMe cable connections and BIOS recognition
questions.explanation: Check connections and BIOS recognition. If recognized in BIOS but not OS, it needs partitioning/formatting.

questions.question: What is RAID 1 protection against?
questions.explanation: RAID 1 mirrors data across two drives so if one fails, the other continues with no data loss.

questions.question: A RAID 1 array shows one drive as failed. What should you do?
options: Take system offline immediately and replace the failed drive
questions.explanation: With one drive failed in RAID 1, you're unprotected. Replace the failed drive immediately to restore redundancy.

questions.question: What is chkdsk used for?
options: Check file system for errors and repair them
questions.explanation: chkdsk (Check Disk) scans the file system for logical and physical errors and can repair many.

questions.question: A drive shows 'disk read error' on startup. What's the likely cause?
options: Bad sectors on the drive or connection issue
questions.explanation: Read errors indicate bad disk sectors or loose SATA connections. Test connections first, then check drive health.

questions.question: A monitor shows no signal. What should you check first?
options: Verify monitor power and cable connections to the computer
questions.explanation: Start with basics: Is the monitor powered on? Is the cable connected securely to both monitor and computer?

questions.question: A display shows only part of the image, cut off on the sides. What's a common cause?
questions.explanation: Overscan settings in display properties or monitor OSD can cut off image edges. Adjust resolution or overscan settings.

questions.question: A display shows flickering. What's the most likely cause?
options: Refresh rate too low or cable interference
questions.explanation: Flickering usually results from low refresh rates (<60Hz) or interference from power cables near the display cable.

questions.question: A laptop screen went black but the system is still running (fans spin, lights on). What should you try?
options: Press Windows+P to change display mode (may be projecting to external)
questions.explanation: External display mode may be active. Windows+P toggles display modes; try keyboard brightness keys too.

questions.question: Colors appear washed out or incorrect. What adjustments might help?
options: Adjust color settings, brightness, contrast in display properties or monitor OSD
questions.explanation: Color issues are often adjustable: monitor settings, graphics driver color adjustments, or display calibration.

questions.question: A smartphone won't charge. What should you check first?
options: Inspect charging port for debris and test with different charger
questions.explanation: First check if the charging port is clean, cable is intact, and charger works with other devices.

questions.question: A mobile device battery drains very quickly. What could cause this?
options: High screen brightness, background apps, or poor signal causing radio to work harder
questions.explanation: Quick battery drain has multiple causes: aging battery, excessive app usage, high screen brightness, weak signal.

questions.question: A touchscreen is unresponsive. What's a good first troubleshooting step?
options: Clean the screen and check if screen protector is too thick
questions.explanation: Dirt, fingerprints, or overly thick screen protectors reduce touch sensitivity. Clean and try removing protector first.

questions.question: A mobile device constantly reboots. What's likely the issue?
options: Software crash loop or hardware issue
questions.explanation: Continuous reboot loops indicate either corrupted software or hardware problems (power delivery, storage).

questions.question: Mobile device apps keep crashing. What should you try first?
options: Uninstall and reinstall the app, clear cache
questions.explanation: Uninstalling/reinstalling and clearing cache often fixes app crashes caused by corrupted app data.

questions.question: A computer cannot connect to the network. What's the first troubleshooting step?
options: Check if network cable is connected
questions.explanation: Always check the physical connection first - is the cable plugged in and indicator lights visible?

questions.question: A device shows limited or no internet connection. What should you check?
options: Check IP configuration and connectivity with ipconfig and ping commands
questions.explanation: Use ipconfig to verify device got an IP address and ping default gateway to test connectivity.

questions.question: Internet works on one computer but not another on the same network. What's likely the issue?
options: Individual computer's network settings or configuration
questions.explanation: If one device works, the network infrastructure is fine. Check the non-working computer's IP, gateway, DNS settings.

questions.question: A device connects to Wi-Fi but has no internet. What should you verify?
questions.explanation: Successful Wi-Fi connection but no internet indicates gateway, DNS, or WAN configuration issues in the router.

questions.question: Network is very slow. What could be the cause?
options: High utilization, interference, driver issues, connection quality
questions.explanation: Slow networks can result from congestion, interference, outdated drivers, or poor signal quality.

questions.question: What does the tracert command help diagnose?
options: Network path and identify where connection is failing
questions.explanation: tracert shows the route packets take to a destination and identifies where the connection fails.

questions.question: A user can't connect to a VPN. What should you check first?
options: VPN client is installed, credentials are correct, and internet connectivity exists
questions.explanation: Verify VPN software is installed, user credentials work, and base internet connectivity is functional.

questions.question: When should you escalate a support ticket?
options: When normal troubleshooting steps don't resolve the issue
questions.explanation: Escalate when your troubleshooting and knowledge limits are reached and higher-level support is needed.

questions.question: What is a workaround in troubleshooting context?
options: Temporary bypass of an issue while a permanent fix is developed
questions.explanation: A workaround provides temporary relief while the root cause is still being investigated or permanent fix is being developed.

questions.question: After fixing an issue, what should you do?
options: Document the solution and verify the fix resolves the original problem
questions.explanation: Always verify the fix works completely and document the solution for future reference.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 5.2 Troubleshooting Motherboards, RAM, CPU & Power
questions.question: What does CPU overheating typically cause?
options: System throttling or shutdown to prevent damage
questions.explanation: CPU thermal protection limits speed (throttling) or shuts down to prevent permanent processor damage.

questions.objective: Core 1 - 5.2 Troubleshooting Motherboards, RAM, CPU & Power
questions.question: A computer powers on but no video output appears. What's a logical first step?
options: Reseat RAM and CPU power connections
questions.explanation: No video with power often means loose connections. Reseat RAM, CPU power, and main power connectors.

questions.question: A partition is marked as RAW instead of NTFS/FAT32. What does this mean?
options: File system is corrupted or damaged
questions.explanation: RAW partition means the file system structure is corrupted. Recovery software may recover data before reformatting.

questions.question: A display has dead pixels (black dots that never light up). What's the only real fix?
options: Replace the display - dead pixels hardware damage cannot be repaired
questions.explanation: Dead pixels are hardware failures at the pixel level. Software cannot fix them - display replacement is required.

questions.question: A phone has been in water. What's the proper response?
options: Power it on immediately to test
Power off immediately and allow to dry completely in dry environment
questions.explanation: Immediately power off a wet device and let it dry for 24-48 hours before powering on again.

questions.question: What should you do if you suspect a network cable is faulty?
options: Test with a known good cable to determine if the problem is cable or device
questions.explanation: Swap the cable with a known working one to isolate whether the problem is the cable or the network port.

questions.question: A user reports an intermittent problem (happens sometimes). What information should you gather?
options: When it happens, what was happening before, frequency, error messages
questions.explanation: Intermittent issues require detailed information about timing, preceding events, and error logs for diagnosis.
